chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Maḥmūdī, from his father, from Yūnus, from Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: “It is obligatory upon the Imam, when he sees a man committing zina or drinking wine, to carry out the hadd punishment upon him, and he does not need evidence along with his own seeing, because he is Allah’s trustee among His creation. And when he sees a man stealing, then it is obligatory upon him to rebuke him, forbid him, move on, and leave him.”
I said: “How is that?” He said: “Because when the right belongs to Allah, then it is obligatory upon the Imam to establish it; and when it belongs to the people, then it belongs to the people.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed authority responsible for establishing judgment
key_terms.الْوَاجِبُ: that which is obligatory and binding

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah’s rights and people’s rights in hadd rulings according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction between rights belonging to Allah and rights belonging to people. It states that the Imam establishes hadd punishments in matters that are Allah’s right when he directly witnesses them, while in matters tied to people’s rights, the claim belongs to those affected.
